summary.text: Define \(y_0=2\), \(y_1=56\), and \(y_{n+2}=-4y_{n+1}-64y_n\); direct expansion shows that \(y_n^2\) satisfies the three-step recurrence \(u_{n+3}=-48u_{n+2}+3072u_{n+1}+262144u_n\). Eliminating intermediate terms from the original recurrence gives the same recurrence for the odd-indexed subsequence, and agreement of the first three values yields equality by induction.

full_proof.text:
Let \((a_n)_{n\ge 0}\) be the integer sequence defined by
\[
a_0=-1,\qquad a_1=4,\qquad a_2=176,\qquad a_3=3136,
\]
and, for every \(r\ge 0\),
\[
a_{r+4}=-4a_{r+3}+256a_{r+1}+4096a_r. \tag{1}
\]
We prove that every odd-indexed term \(a_{2n+1}\) is a square.

Define an auxiliary integer sequence \((y_n)_{n\ge 0}\) by
\[
y_0=2,\qquad y_1=56,
\]
and
\[
y_{n+2}=-4y_{n+1}-64y_n\qquad(n\ge 0). \tag{2}
\]
We will prove the stronger identity
\[
a_{2n+1}=y_n^2 \qquad(n\ge 0). \tag{3}
\]

First, we derive a recurrence for terms of \(a\) whose indices have the same parity. Applying (1) at three consecutive positions gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{r+4}&=-4a_{r+3}+256a_{r+1}+4096a_r, \
a_{r+5}&=-4a_{r+4}+256a_{r+2}+4096a_{r+1}, \
a_{r+6}&=-4a_{r+5}+256a_{r+3}+4096a_{r+2}.
\end{aligned} \tag{4}
\]
Substituting the second equation into the third yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{r+6}
&=-4\bigl(-4a_{r+4}+256a_{r+2}+4096a_{r+1}\bigr)
  +256a_{r+3}+4096a_{r+2}\\
&=16a_{r+4}+3072a_{r+2}+256a_{r+3}-16384a_{r+1}. \tag{5}
\end{aligned}
\]
On the other hand, multiplying the first equation in (4) by \(64\) and rearranging gives
\[
256a_{r+3}-16384a_{r+1}=-64a_{r+4}+262144a_r. \tag{6}
\]
Using (6) in (5), we obtain
\[
a_{r+6}=-48a_{r+4}+3072a_{r+2}+262144a_r \qquad(r\ge 0). \tag{7}
\]
Thus the subsequence of odd-indexed terms satisfies a third-order recurrence with coefficients \(-48,3072,262144\).

We now show that the squares \(y_n^2\) satisfy the same recurrence. From (2),
\[
y_{n+2}=-4y_{n+1}-64y_n
\]
and
\[
y_{n+3}=-4y_{n+2}-64y_{n+1}. \tag{8}
\]
Write \(x=y_n\) and \(z=y_{n+1}\). Then
\[
y_{n+2}=-64x-4z,
\]
and substituting this into (8) gives
\[
y_{n+3}=-4(-64x-4z)-64z=256x-48z.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
-48y_{n+2}^2+3072y_{n+1}^2+262144y_n^2
&=-48(-64x-4z)^2+3072z^2+262144x^2\\
&=-48(4096x^2+512xz+16z^2)+3072z^2+262144x^2\\
&=65536x^2-24576xz+2304z^2\\
&=(256x-48z)^2\\
&=y_{n+3}^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore
\[
y_{n+3}^2=-48y_{n+2}^2+3072y_{n+1}^2+262144y_n^2
\qquad(n\ge 0). \tag{9}
\]

It remains to compare initial values and then induct. For \(n=0\),
\[
a_1=4=2^2=y_0^2.
\]
For \(n=1\),
\[
a_3=3136=56^2=y_1^2.
\]
For the third initial value, first use (1) to calculate
\[
a_4=-4a_3+256a_1+4096a_0
=-4(3136)+256(4)+4096(-1)=-15616.
\]
Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_5
&=-4a_4+256a_2+4096a_1\\
&=-4(-15616)+256(176)+4096(4)\\
&=123904.
\end{aligned}
\]
Meanwhile, (2) gives
\[
y_2=-4y_1-64y_0=-4(56)-64(2)=-352,
\]
so
\[
y_2^2=(-352)^2=123904=a_5.
\]
Thus (3) holds for \(n=0,1,2\).

Now suppose that for some \(n\ge 0\) the identities
\[
a_{2n+1}=y_n^2,\qquad
 a_{2n+3}=y_{n+1}^2,\qquad
 a_{2n+5}=y_{n+2}^2
\]
have already been established. Apply (7) with \(r=2n+1\). Since
\[
r+2=2n+3,\qquad r+4=2n+5,\qquad r+6=2n+7,
\]
we get
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{2n+7}
&=-48a_{2n+5}+3072a_{2n+3}+262144a_{2n+1}\\
&=-48y_{n+2}^2+3072y_{n+1}^2+262144y_n^2\\
&=y_{n+3}^2,
\end{aligned}
\]
where the final equality is (9). Starting from the three base cases, this induction proves
\[
a_{2n+1}=y_n^2
\]
for every nonnegative integer \(n\).

Since each \(y_n\) is an integer, \(a_{2n+1}\) is the square of an integer for every \(n\ge 0\). Hence every odd-indexed term of A113254 is a perfect square.
